corrections.source_says: The main experiment is within-participant and counterbalanced, but random allocation is not stated anywhere in the document. The online_rct label is therefore unsupported; use other with an explicit description of the counterbalanced experiment and unreported allocation method, retaining assignment.randomized='not_stated' and criterion_1_random_assignment_of_ai='unclear'.
corrections.quote: To mitigate task order effects, task order and AI assistance were counterbalanced (Latin-square style).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4, Counterbalancing and Assignment; p. 9, Section 4

corrections.source_says: Appendix A is included in this PDF on pp. 17-18 and contains the analytical and creative task prompts and their fixed AI suggestions. Record this included appendix as exists='yes', in_this_pdf=true, with its location and contents; it contains no additional statistical tables. No separate external supplement is identified.
corrections.quote: The specific task prompts and the AI suggestion used in both conditions are provided in Appendix A.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4; pp. 17-18, Appendix A, Task Prompts and AI Suggestions

corrections.form_value: Only the main experiment (S1) and think-aloud evaluation (S2) are listed.
corrections.source_says: Section 3.3 also reports a pilot experiment in two iterations: a time-limited pilot with 5 participants and an untimed iteration with 11 participants. Add the pilot phases to the study inventory, identifying them as design-development work without reported outcome estimates; separate randomized and analyzed counts are not stated and should remain null. The pilot data were not evidence for the main experiment, and these counts must not be added to its 47 analyzed participants.
corrections.quote: We then conducted an untimed iteration with 11 participants using revised prompts and incentives. The pilot data were used solely to inform the design change and were not treated as evidence for the main experiment.

corrections.source_says: Populate the dedicated exclusions field with the 7 participants excluded after data collection for external-tool use, leaving 47 analyzed from 54 recruited. These numbers are already correctly recorded in participants.who, but exclusions is empty; 54 is a recruitment count, not a stated randomized count.
corrections.quote: We recruited a total of 54 participants on Prolific. After data collection, we excluded 7 participants who used external tools, resulting in 47 valid participants.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 3.4, opening paragraph; p. 5, Section 3.2, external-tool screening

confirmed: The complete markdown was read, including references and Appendix A. The PDF is 18 pages and identifies arXiv:2605.15322v1 [cs.HC], 14 May 2026, with FAccT 2026 DOI 10.1145/3805689.3812389; the recorded title and authors match (PDF p. 1).
The main study recruited 54 people, excluded 7, and analyzed 47; n_randomized=null is appropriate because no randomized denominator is reported (PDF p. 6, Section 3.4).

The same 47 people completed a task with and a task without assistance; the two arm counts do not represent separate participant groups or increase the eligibility denominator (PDF p. 10, Section 4.1, Self-Reported Usage and Qualitative Analysis).

There is no confirmed randomized study with an eligible creativity or cross-person diversity outcome: the four computed measures compare each response with the task-specific AI suggestion (PDF pp. 6-8, Section 3.4; p. 13, Section 5).

Eligibility core='no', criterion_2='not_met', criterion_3='not_met', and context_class='none' are supported under the codebook: the main analysis is below 50 people and measures AI-text adoption, not creativity or diversity across writers (PDF pp. 6-8, Section 3.4).
All means, SDs, differences, p-values and standardized effects in S1-O1.contrasts[0].reported exactly match the Jaccard rows (PDF p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Table 2).
All means, SDs, differences, p-values and standardized effects in S1-O2.contrasts[0].reported exactly match the POS TF-ISF cosine rows (PDF p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Table 2).
All means, SDs, differences, p-values and standardized effects in S1-O3.contrasts[0].reported exactly match the SBERT rows (PDF p. 10, Table 1; p. 11, Table 2).

Table 1 uses paired-samples tests and Cohen's dz; Table 2 uses independent-samples tests and Cohen's d, as the form states (PDF pp. 10-11, table captions and column headings; p. 8, Statistical hypothesis tests).

Every number in the one-line finding matches Table 1, including aspect sentiment match 0.092 versus 0.040, p=0.004; the stronger analytical-task pattern is explicitly described (PDF pp. 9-11, Sections 4 and 4.1, Tables 1-2).

The task descriptions match the O. Henry story, analytical direct-answer suggestion, and creative scaffold for rewriting the ending from Jimmy Wells's perspective (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 3.1 and 3.4; pp. 17-18, Appendix A).

Figure 1 visibly labels the suggestion GPT 4.5, while the main-study methods do not explicitly identify the generating model; the form preserves that distinction (PDF p. 7, Figure 1; pp. 5-8, Methods).

The follow-up has 4 university students, a three-paragraph task on a chosen topic, and permission to use any LLM; it is an illustrative think-aloud evaluation, not a randomized comparison with reported creativity/diversity scores (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2; pp. 8-9, Section 3.5; p. 11, Section 4.2).

This is an original empirical paper, not a synthesis; no study-pooling count, pooled estimate, confidence interval or standardization target is reported for a meta-analysis (PDF pp. 5-14, Methods, Results and Discussion).
summary: The reported numbers and exclusion from the core dataset are supported: the main study analyzed 47 people, did not state random assignment, and measured AI-text adoption rather than creativity or cross-writer diversity. Correct the unsupported RCT label, appendix record, omitted pilot phases, and empty exclusions field.
